title: Istanbul's Three Shores
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Classify twelve Istanbul places as on the historic peninsula, in Galata, or on the Asian shore, then see each one appear on a satellite map.

learningObjectives: Classify twelve Istanbul places by the shore they stand on (the historic peninsula, Galata, or the Asian shore), with at least 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then reveal (classification on a map)
keyQuestions: Which body of water separates Europe from Asia in Istanbul?
Which body of water separates the historic peninsula from Galata?
Why do the Byzantine and early Ottoman monuments cluster on one shore?
commonMisconceptions: All of Istanbul is in Europe.
The Golden Horn is part of the Bosphorus, so Galata is in Asia.
The old Greek city of Byzantium stood where the modern city center (Taksim) is.
The walls of Constantinople run along the Bosphorus.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on twelve places (mastery: 10 of 12).
Name the water crossed and the continent reached on the Eminönü to Kadıköy ferry.
